content:
Sarah: Good morning, CoverWatch Insurance, this is Sarah. How can I help you?

Mike: Hey, good morning. My name's Mike Torres. I got your number from a buddy of mine — Danny Ortiz, you helped him with his plumbing company last year?

Sarah: Oh yeah, Danny! Great guy. How's he doing?

Mike: He's good, business is booming for him. He said you guys did a great job getting his rates down so I figured I'd give you a call. We've got our renewal coming up and I'm not happy with what we're paying.

Sarah: Happy to help. Let me get some basics first. What's the name of your business?

Mike: Coastal Roofing LLC. We also sometimes go by Coastal Roof & Repair — that's kind of our DBA for the residential side of things. Same entity though, just a marketing thing.

Sarah: Got it. And you're the owner?

Mike: Yeah, sole owner. Started the company back in 2018. Was doing roofing work for other people for about ten years before that and finally decided to go out on my own. Best decision I ever made, honestly.

Sarah: That's great. Tell me about what you guys do.

Mike: So we're a full-service roofing company. We do residential and commercial — new installs, tear-offs, repairs, maintenance contracts. We're based in Wilmington, North Carolina. Mostly work within about a 60-mile radius, so we cover the whole Cape Fear region. We've been picking up more commercial work lately — just landed a big HOA contract for a condo development, that's been keeping us busy.

Sarah: Nice. What's your office address?

Mike: 1420 Marine Drive, Suite B, Wilmington. Zip is 28401. It's not fancy — it's basically where the office staff works and where the crews meet up in the morning before heading to job sites. We've got a yard out back where we keep materials and the trucks.

Sarah: Perfect. And your FEIN?

Mike: Yeah, let me pull that up... one second... okay, it's 12-3456789.

Sarah: Thanks. How about revenue — what did you guys do last year?

Mike: So last year was a good year. We did about two and a half million, maybe a little over. Honestly I'd have to check with my bookkeeper for the exact number — I'm more of a "go out and get the work done" guy, you know? But it was definitely north of two million. That HOA contract I mentioned came in Q3 and that pushed us up quite a bit.

Sarah: Understood. And how many employees do you have?

Mike: Right now we've got about 45 people total. It fluctuates — roofing is seasonal, obviously. In the dead of winter we might be down to 30. But right now, spring into summer, we're fully staffed. I'd say roughly 35 full-time guys — those are my crew leads, the experienced roofers, the office staff, our estimator — and then about 10 part-timers we bring on for bigger jobs or when we've got multiple projects running.

Sarah: Got it. What about payroll — do you know what your annual payroll was last year?

Mike: Ugh, I should know that off the top of my head. I want to say around... one-point-seven? One-point-eight? Somewhere in there. My bookkeeper would kill me for not knowing the exact number. Actually, can I get back to you on that? I don't want to give you a wrong number and screw up the quotes.

Sarah: Absolutely, no rush on that one. So what coverage are you looking for?

Mike: Okay so we need general liability for sure — that's the big one. With residential work especially, you drop a tool off a roof onto somebody's car, you know, stuff happens. We also need workers comp — obviously, with roofing, that's not optional. We've had a couple incidents. And commercial auto — we've got about 12 trucks. Mix of pickups and some bigger flatbeds for hauling materials.

Sarah: Do you currently have coverage?

Mike: Yeah, we're with Hartford right now. Been with them for three years. The coverage is fine but every year the premiums go up and up. We went from paying $85,000 the first year to over $110,000 this year for basically the same coverage. I don't get it. Our policy expires September 1st so I want to have something lined up well before that.

Sarah: Makes sense. Have you had any claims in the last three years?

Mike: Yeah, two. First one was about two years ago — one of my crew leads, Ricky, he fell off a ladder on a job site. Broke his arm pretty bad, needed surgery. That was a workers comp claim, came out to about $30,000 when it was all said and done. The other one was last year — one of our trucks backed into a client's fence while we were doing a job at their house. That was an auto claim, about $15,000. Homeowner was cool about it, we fixed the fence too, but the insurance still had to pay out. So about $45,000 total over three years.

Sarah: Okay, that's not bad for a roofing company honestly.

Mike: Yeah, we're pretty safety-conscious. I make all my guys do training every quarter. It's an investment but it pays off.

Sarah: That's great to hear. Anything else I should know about the business?

Mike: Let me think... oh, we do some gutter work too. Not a huge part of our revenue but we do gutters as part of roof installs. And we've started doing some solar panel mounting — not the electrical work, just the mounting and roof prep. That's newer, maybe 5% of our work right now but growing.

Sarah: Good to know. What's the best way to reach you?

Mike: Email is probably best — mike.torres@coastalroofing.com. And my cell is 910-555-0173. I'm usually on job sites during the day so I might not pick up right away but I'll call back.

Sarah: Perfect. I think I have enough to start putting together some options. I'll probably have some follow-up questions once I start the applications.

Mike: Sounds good. Oh, one thing I forgot — we do have a mailing address that's different from the office. Can you send stuff to our PO Box? It's PO Box 9102, Wilmington, NC 28402. My office manager checks that daily but sometimes stuff gets lost at the shop.

Sarah: Noted. I'll be in touch within a few days.

Mike: Great, thanks Sarah. Danny was right, you guys are easy to work with.
